paper.title: Instruct2Act: Mapping Multi-modality Instructions to Robotic Actions with Large Language Model
paper.central_claim: Instruct2Act uses an LLM to generate Python programs that call SAM/CLIP and robot primitives to map multi-modality instructions to actions, and this zero-shot approach outperforms many learning-based policies in several tasks (comparable average to VIMA on VIMABench).
paper.scope_decision: in_scope (A): an LLM writes Python that composes SAM/CLIP perception and pick-and-place primitives to control a simulated tabletop arm in VIMABench, closed loop.

preliminary_judgment: Written after reading the fixed text, before opening this paper's seat records: system_method; VIMABench 6 meta-tasks, 150 instances x 3 seeds, simulator final-state success; baselines (VIMA/Gato/Flamingo/DT) copied from the VIMA paper rather than rerun; no same-LLM alternative harness (CaP) although the gap is framed against CaP; in-context examples cover all evaluated task families; processing ablation (51.0 -> 83.0 -> 84.1) on the same tasks; L2/L3 values figure-only; regeneration on interpreter errors not counted; means only; cost acknowledged but unquantified. Expected online, scoped; G weak to moderate, E.causality weak.

gap.author_gap: CaP-style policy code is restricted by the perception APIs and struggles with long/complex commands; no general system covers multi-modality instructions without training.
gap.checked_gap: The CaP limitation is asserted, but no CaP (or any LLM-code) baseline is run; the only baselines are trained policies copied from VIMA. What is verified is that an LLM+SAM+CLIP program can reach the VIMA-20M average on six VIMABench tasks.
lineage: Code as Policies / VISPROG / ViperGPT (LLM writes programs over APIs) -> Instruct2Act (robot-hierarchy API prompt, SAM+CLIP perception, multimodal retrieval, processing modules)
CLIPort / Perceiver-Actor / VIMA (trained instruction-conditioned manipulation policies) = the compared class

closest_adjacent.name: Code as Policies (CaP)
closest_adjacent.solved: LLM writes robot policy code from in-context examples
closest_adjacent.unsolved_per_authors: limited by perception APIs, long complex commands

gap.residue: Whether LLM-composed programs beat other LLM-code harnesses, and how much of the success comes from the hand-tailored prompt examples and processing modules versus the LLM, is not separated.
gap.stakes: Training-free language/vision-conditioned manipulation; foundation-model upgrades could transfer for free.
gap.method_response: Provide a robot-hierarchy API prompt with whole-program examples, bolt on perception post-processing, and route all instruction modalities through CLIP retrieval.
gap.remaining_gap: Compute cost, only pick/place primitives, simulation only (authors); no CaP comparison, no real robot, no seed variance (ours).
gap.unresolved: Neighbour papers (CaP, VISPROG, VIMA) are not pinned in the batch materials, so lineage rests on this paper's own citations; empty retrieval does not prove novelty.
gap.aggregate_note: son55 gap retained: the CaP limitation is asserted, not tested; what is verified is parity with VIMA-20M on six L1 tasks.

claims.text: An LLM that writes Python programs over SAM/CLIP/pick-place APIs achieves training-free multimodal-instruction manipulation competitive with learned policies.
claims.setting: VIMABench (PyBullet), 6 meta-tasks, L1; text-davinci-003; SAM-H + CLIP-H
claims.baseline_control: DT-20M, Gato-20M, Flamingo-20M, VIMA-20M numbers copied from VIMA paper; no LLM-code baseline
claims.selection_vs_test: prompt examples cover all six evaluated task families; no separate selection split
claims.result_denominator: 150 instances x 3 seeds per meta-task; L1 average 84.4 vs 84.4 (VIMA); task-wise 91.3/81.4/98.2/78.5/72.0/85.2
claims.allowed_conclusion: On six VIMABench L1 tasks the program-writing harness matches VIMA-20M's average (lower on 4 tasks, higher on 2); superiority over learned policies is not established.

claims.text: Processing modules make zero-shot SAM usable for grasping.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Mask post-processing carries almost all of the perception gain; image pre-processing alone does nothing.

claims.text: The approach generalizes to L2 (combinatorial) and L3 (novel object) levels with small fluctuation.
claims.result_denominator: numbers only in Fig 5 (image); text asserts 'positive results across all levels'
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported only; cannot be audited from the fixed text.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop simulator-judged success with counts. The harness prompt was built for the evaluated task families, there is no new embodiment/simulator and no real robot, so it is not transfer (EVIDENCE rule 2).

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On six VIMABench L1 tasks (PyBullet) an LLM program harness over SAM/CLIP/pick-place reaches the same 84.4% average as the trained VIMA-20M (baseline numbers copied), with mask post-processing worth +32 points; superiority, L2/L3 retention, generality and low cost are not established.

G.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 3). The limitation of CaP (bounded by its perception APIs, weak on long/complex commands) is real and sourced, and the target (training-free multimodal-instruction manipulation) is clear. But the gap is never tested against CaP or any LLM-code neighbour; the only comparison is with trained policies copied from VIMA (agg:E001). The claimed residual ("generate decision-making actions that reduce the error rate", unlike CaP) is not made checkable, so per the G anchor the neighbour comparison and residual are incomplete -> 2.

M.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. The mechanism is concrete and reconstructible (LLM writes main() over SAM/CLIP retrieval, Hungarian matching, Pixel2Loc and PickPlace) and has a causal story for perception failures (shadows, holes, duplicate masks) that the processing ablation matches. Not 4: the central prediction against CaP is never tested, and the in-context examples nearly template the evaluated programs.

X.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Full prompt, API hierarchy, processing steps, pointing mode and retrieval are specified (App A.1-A.3), so the chain is rebuildable. The processing thresholds, the regeneration-on-exception policy and its count, and the image-to-robot transform are not given, and there is no failure or hand-back handling.

measurement.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Simulator-judged final-state success with an explicit protocol (150 instances per meta-task, three seeds) and per-task L1 numbers for six tasks. Not 4: L2/L3 values are figure-only (Table 2 averages over levels), single-modal results cover 3/6 tasks, the LLaMA-Adapter result uses 40 instances, the baselines are copied rather than measured under this protocol, and the regeneration-on-error attempts behind each success are not counted (agg:E002).

causality.reason: Both seats 2; confirmed. One-at-a-time processing toggles (51.0 -> 50.0 / 83.0 / 84.1) and SAM/CLIP size sweeps hold the LLM fixed. But there is no CaP or other LLM-code harness, no LLM-free fixed-template program, and the prompt covers every evaluated task family (agg:E003); "prompt + SAM + CLIP template" remains a strong alternative explanation for the parity with VIMA.

holdout.reason: Both seats 2; confirmed. VIMABench L2/L3 are held-out placements/objects relative to VIMA's training, but for this harness the prompt was written to cover the same task families (EVIDENCE rule 2), L4 novel tasks are excluded, contamination is not discussed, and the L2/L3 numbers cannot be audited from text.

statistics.reason: Both seats 2; confirmed. Three seeds x 150 instances support the means; no variance/CI, no paired statistics and no failure breakdown.

cost.reason: Both seats 1; confirmed. High computational cost is acknowledged in Limitations; no calls, tokens, latency, GPU-hours or regeneration counts; no matched-budget comparison.
